instruction.what: Step 2.1, the structure of one subgroup (stage 1, B3): what stands with the subgroup's words in each verse, read from the stored structure. One item at a time: double-meaning (a surface with more than one code), qualifier (negators and the word each reaches, adjectives, adverbs, prepositional qualifiers), entity (who is named or referred to), direction (from whom to whom, by the grammar), pairing (one row for each partner collection: its words in the verses shared with the subgroup). Nothing here says what anything does for the inner being; that begins at step 3.1.
read: Take one row at a time (`rows`): what it asks, its occurrences (`as`: member, the subgroup's word; partner, the other word), and its verses.

Read each verse (`verses`) from its stored structure, one line for each word: * marks an occurrence of the subgroup; then the position, surface, Strong's code and morph, and what the pairing makes of the word (its type, the qualifier it carries, a negator, a party, the collections of a word of another collection). Nothing is evaluated that is not stored.
Where each word stands: its side and distance from the subgroup's word, from the positions. Adjacency is not scope: a negator or qualifier is read for the word it reaches by the grammar.
A pairing row shows the WordNet control for its partner collection: a pairing WordNet gives and the verses do not show is one to look for; a pairing only the verses show has no control.
Differences in meaning are read from the base data (the Strong's code, the morph, the construction), not from the English alone. The subgroup's 1.1 senses (`senses`) are what the findings build on.
write: Fill `answer.rows`: for each row, disposition observed with its `findings`, or none with its `reason` (where the row allows none: nothing of the item stands with the subgroup in its verses).

One finding for each distinct thing the structure shows; the same finding in several verses is ONE finding naming all its occurrences; a verse that shows something different is its own finding. Together the findings name every occurrence of the row (occurrence ids or verse references), each in one finding.

kind: as the template gives it (pairing; relation for direction; face for double-meaning). obs_text: concise; names the verses it holds in, as the package writes the references (for example Act 18:4); states what the structure shows (which word, where it stands, what it reaches or gives by the grammar); never a verse restated, never what it does for the inner being.
basis: stated (the verse says it) or read (read from the structure), with `grounds`: words copied exactly from the verses it is tied to (the record checks them).
Each subgroup's surface has its own finding; none joins two subgroups. A data error is named in grounds, not fixed.

`older`: answer each older observation shown under the row, once: keep (with `nature`), restate (with `nature`, `new_text`, `checked`), merge (with `into`), consume (with `carriers` ["this"] or observation ids, and `mapping`), delete_neither (with `reason`), carry (with `to` and `reason`), defer (with `collection`, `nature`, `finding`). One listed under another row is answered there.
Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordStructure -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview). The record refuses the whole file on any fault and lists every fault.

keep.text: Morph is read, not carried: where occurrences of a word show different stems or voices, record whether the subject does, undergoes or causes the act.

A word that is only a homonym or a name, with no meaningful context, is recorded as such (tag no-human-context) and left. Data errors found while reading are flagged (tag data-error), not fixed in the reading.

A word is read per its lettered Strong's code (its grain), never the bare lemma (B:113). The occurrences of a word with several senses are related per grain and never aggregated across grains: related verses are same-grain occurrences.
One observation per finding, never a duplicate description; a finding applying to several verses or words carries several nodes, each with the word's role in it.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Where the evidence points to more than one reading, each is its own observation with its own evidence.
A re-read includes the observations already recorded for the verse, so the reading sees prior findings and builds on them.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

Every older live observation with a live node on an occurrence of the row (a stage that is not the build's own) is answered in fill.older when the row is recorded, once: keep or restate (each with its marker), merge into a named observation, consume (live observations carry its meaning, stated in words, verified before it is deleted), delete as neither (comment first), or defer to a named collection (marked now; only the finding is left to that collection). An observation already marked by the validation, answered in a build or deferred is not asked again. A new observation whose text equals that of another live observation of the collection is refused, the other named. LayerCheck re-derives both from the tables. The end state of a collection's build is that every observation of its scope is marked and fixed or deleted, every word node complete or with its reason, and each deferral owned by a named collection.

When a verse is worked, every existing observation and node on it, of any stage, is checked against the verse by its wording. The stage is not an indication of the nature of an observation and is never used to filter. Each observation is accepted, modified (changed in place; the old value, the new value and the reason are kept in ib_observation_change), soft deleted (the `deleted` column, with the reason), merged (a duplicate description, into the observation that is kept) or, when its wording shows it is not verse understanding, left exactly as it is with the reason. The check's fixes are part of it and need no separate approval. Nothing is physically deleted.

The nodes of a layer observation are the occurrences the aspect demands (a word's occurrences, the group's occurrences, the partner's occurrences in the verses they share), written by the recorder with the collection and the subgroup of each surface; they are never typed. An item answered by senses (word-sense) names, for each sense, the occurrences it holds for, and together the senses cover every occurrence; the recorder checks them against the data. The interpretation is the observation text, founded in what the evidence shows (basis stated or read, B:131) and tied to its verses (the text names them and does not restate them): the items of every step (S1, 1.1, 1.2, 2.1) state what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show of a word and never what a word does for the inner being; their nodes carry the role lexical and no route. The whole file is checked and written in one transaction; any problem refuses all of it. A row answered again withdraws its earlier observations with the reason.

An aspect is recorded as none only where its item allows it (cfg_setting layer.reading none_allowed) and with its reason in words. A group definition and a group's Strong's enrichment are always observed.

A node is on one occurrence (verse_lexical_id) and carries the collection of its surface (a supportive node, the collection of the surface it supports); a node already on the observation for the same occurrence is not written twice, and takes the role. A node with no collection to carry, or on a verse out of scope (B:130), is not written and is listed.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

senses.text: Considering a matter: turning attention and thought to it, looking it over, setting the heart on it. The Lord asks Satan whether he has fixed on Job, the observer sets his heart on the field and takes instruction, the Preacher looks over all his works, the generation gives no thought to the servant's being cut off, the sinner sees his transgressions and turns, the seer contemplates the horns, Joseph turns over what he resolved, and Abraham fixes his attention on his own body without his faith weakening. In each the consideration is an act of the mind taking in a matter, usually before a turn or a conclusion. Verses: Job 1:8, Job 2:3, Pro 24:32, Ecc 2:11, Isa 53:8, Eze 18:28, Dan 7:8, Mat 1:20, Rom 4:19.

Reckoning something or someone as a certain thing: how a person or thing is counted, judged or esteemed. Sarah counts the promiser faithful, Abraham concludes that God can raise the dead, Moses counts the reproach of Christ greater than treasure, rulers are held to be rulers, the silent fool is held wise, silver is counted as nothing, the men are counted reliable, the people are counted as foreigners, as sheep, as pots, the laws as strange, the potter as clay, the disciples dispute who is held greatest, the uncircumcised is counted as circumcised, servants are counted as masters worthy of honor, the Lord counts the exiles good. The word is a reckoning or valuation, the standing given by a judgment. Verses: 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20, Neh 13:13, Pro 17:28, Mar 10:42, Heb 11:11, Heb 11:19, Heb 11:26, Lev 19:23, 1Sa 1:16, Jer 24:5, 1Cor 4:1, 2Th 3:15, 1Ti 6:1, 1Pe 5:12, Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Isa 29:16, Isa 29:17, Lam 4:2, Hos 8:12, Luk 22:24, Rom 2:26, Rom 8:36.

Having regard: giving notice and heed to someone or something, or refusing it. The Lord has no regard for Cain's offering, the psalmist asks God to have regard for the covenant and the vine, the wicked do not regard the Lord's works, God does not regard those wise in their own conceit, Levi disregards his kin, the righteous have regard for the life of the beast, the Medes have no regard for silver, and none is shown to the priests. The word is attention that turns toward a person or matter with favor or care, or is withheld. Verses: Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9, Deu 9:27, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, 2Ki 3:14, 2Ch 5:11, 2Ch 6:19, Job 9:21, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14, Psa 119:117, Psa 144:3, Pro 12:10, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16.

'With regard to' as a linking phrase of respect: it marks the matter spoken of, a festival or a sect or the children of man or the Philistines. The words are prepositions and nouns of concern and carry no act of thinking. Verses: Judg 15:3, Ecc 3:18, Act 28:22, Col 2:16.

Regarding by a standard: Paul says he knew and took account of Christ once by the standard of the flesh and now takes account of no one by it. The Greek verbs are of knowing, used for the rule by which a person is judged. Verses: 2Cor 5:16.

Weighing in the mind: the prophets' words are to be weighed by the others who judge them, and the Preacher weighs, studies and arranges proverbs. The word is an act of testing and judging what is said or learned. Verses: 1Cor 14:29, Ecc 12:9.

Weighing out metal on scales: the traders weigh out silver, and the gifts are to be weighed before the priests. It is the act of measuring by weight, with no act of thinking. Verses: Ezr 8:29, Zep 1:11.

Weight as a stated measure: a ring and bracelets of a given weight in shekels, a bar of gold of fifty shekels, and the balances of the hair. The word is the weight of an object. Verses: Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21, Eze 5:1.

rows.subject: heart
rows.asks: Which words of this partner collection stand with the subgroup's surfaces in the verses they share, where does each stand (side and distance, from the stored structure), and which stand out? The WordNet control for this collection is shown. Write one finding for each distinct thing the structure shows; a finding holds the verses it holds in as its nodes.

older.text: Qohelet's heart reasons to the shared breath, then leaves the spirit's destination open (Ecc 3:18–21). This is the fullest statement that the breath does not mark man off from beast (§1.1). It is also the place where the difference is left unknown rather than denied.

c. Inner speech — the heart as the place one "says" things: "Said in his heart / to himself": Gen 17:17; 24:45; 27:41; 1Ki 12:26; 1Sa 27:1; Deu 7:17; 8:17; 9:4; 18:21; Psa 10:6, 11, 13; 14:1; 53:1; Isa 14:13; 47:8, 10; 49:21; Jer 5:24; 13:22; Obd 3; Zep 1:12; 2:15; Est 6:6; Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Rom 10:6; Rev 18:7.; Hannah "was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved" (1Sa 1:13).; "Before I had finished speaking in my heart" (Gen 24:45).; The *content* of heart-speech is often self-assessment or self-deception: "I shall not be moved" (Psa 10:6); "There is no God" (Psa 14:1); "My power … has gotten me this wealth" (Deu 8:17); "I am, and there is no one besides me" (Isa 47:8; Zep 2:15).; Nehemiah "took counsel with *myself*" (Neh 5:7, lēv); "Ask *yourself*" style reflexives also appear.

What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)

older.text: Part 2 verses: what they add: The body's end of rivalrous anger: "The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away; the desire of the wicked will perish!" (Psa 112:10). What he sees is the righteous man, whose "horn is exalted in honor" (112:9). Seeing the rival's rise ends in the angry one dissolving, not in the spear of 1Sa 18; Contrast seat: "His heart is steady; he will not be afraid" (112:8), said of the righteous one, two verses before. The seat is again named in the one the anger is aimed at (see Neh 4:6 above). Genuine; Rivalry among the disciples: "when the ten heard it, they were indignant at the two brothers" (Mat 20:24 = Mar 10:41). What they heard was Jesus's answer about the two brothers' place: "to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant" (Mat 20:23; Mar 10:40); Jesus answers by redefining greatness: "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them … It shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant" (Mat 20:25–26; Mar 10:42–43); The anger at a rival's rise is not rebuked directly. The standing it is about is re-defined, so the rise it resented no longer counts. This is a reframing, the §9 and §6 move used on rivalry; Seat : none in-verse.
